title: Multi-tenant events table (millions of rows): BRIN, composite, partial and covering indexes under RLS
issue: An RLS tenant filter turns time-range scans, 'latest N' and hot-kind lookups into questions of which index the planner may still use: a tiny tenant cannot profit from created_at order, a subject with many tenants cannot profit from the (tenant_id, created_at) btree, and jsonb @> is not leakproof.
symptom: latest_n and hot_kind walk a time-ordered index and discard other tenants' rows for tiny subjects; broad subjects lose BRIN/covering index-only scans to the policy filter.

scale.meaning: rows in app.events spread over 10 days. Tenants = scale/2500 with skewed sizes (tenant 1 ~8% of rows).

subjects.name: selective
subjects.note: member of the smallest tenant only (~800 rows at 5M)

subjects.name: mid
subjects.note: member of 10 mid-size tenants (~20k rows at 5M)

subjects.name: big_tenant
subjects.note: member of tenant 1 only (~8% of rows)

subjects.name: many
subjects.note: member of 2/3 of all tenants (1333 at default scale)
